title: so-n6b.1 never says which files count as 'exist now', so the literal reading expires every profile always
description:
Raised while settling so-n6b.11. That issue settled WHO owns the expiry blind spot (jr5.2, via a third input to downwind_of); this one is WHAT goes in that input, which so-n6b.11 deliberately left open.

so-n6b.1 says to compare 'the set of files that exist now' against measured_files and the import graph, with the acceptance criterion 'a file exists in the repository that is absent from both measured_files and the import graph'. It never names the enumerator or its scope.

Taken literally that expires every profile on every run, forever, on a repository nobody has touched. measured_files comes from coverage.py's file table (profiler/coverage_db.py:252, 310), so it holds Python source under the --cov scope; ImportGraph holds Python modules. README.md, pyproject.toml, .gitignore, every fixture and every data file EXIST and are absent from both. So does a fresh clone's whole non-Python tree. Divergence would never be observed, because the profile is born expired.

Scoping to Python is necessary but not sufficient. A .py file in a directory coverage never measures -- scripts/, tooling, a vendored tree, an example -- is equally unknown to the maps, and stays unknown no matter how many times the profile is regenerated. Under the naive rule that pins the profile to expired permanently: every run takes the full-suite path, so-jr5.3's instrumented fallback rewrites the profile, and the very next run is expired again. The tool would never select anything, and would look like it was working.

Note this is NOT the same as jr5.2's 'a changed path that is not Python' blind spot. That one is about a file you CHANGED and is a deliberate MVP shortcut so-n6b.4 removes. This is about files that merely EXIST and that you did not touch, which is the entire basis of so-n6b.1's divergence test.

The scope must therefore be derived from the same configuration the profiling run used, so that 'known to the maps' and 'in scope for expiry' cannot drift apart -- a file in scope must be one a regenerated profile WOULD know. Candidate sources: the --cov targets, the pytest testpaths/rootdir, or a scope recorded into the profile at capture time so the check cannot disagree with the run that produced it. Which of those, and whether the scope is stored in the profile or recomputed, is the call.

Whatever is chosen also fixes so-n6b.1's acceptance criterion, which currently states the unscoped comparison, and names what so-jr5.4 must enumerate to build existing_files.
acceptance_criteria: The set of files compared against the maps has a defined scope, and a defined source for that scope. A file that is in scope is one that a freshly regenerated profile would know, so a profile regenerated against an unchanged tree is NOT expired -- demonstrated by a test that regenerates and asserts not-expired. A non-Python file, and a Python file outside the profiling scope, do not on their own expire a profile. so-n6b.1's acceptance criterion is rewritten to state the scoped comparison. Settled before so-n6b.1 is implemented.
close_reason:
Settled by the epic owner. The set of files compared against the maps is scoped, and the scope is RECORDED IN THE PROFILE AT CAPTURE TIME.

THE SCOPE is the coverage targets union the pytest test paths, as actually resolved by the profiling run, written into ProfilingData alongside so-746's repo root. IN SCOPE means a .py file under those roots, enumerated by plain 'git ls-files' -- tracked files only. On this repository the roots are {smoke_optimiser, tests}, putting 38 files in scope and leaving out scripts/branch_summary.py, smoke_optimiser/py.typed and the 13 tracked root files.

WHY RECORDED RATHER THAN RECOMPUTED: config.cov_source is not reliably what was measured. runner.py:290-298 appends --cov={cov_source} only when config.pytest_args lacks a --cov, and nothing anywhere inspects the project's own [tool.pytest.ini_options] addopts -- pytest applies those itself, invisibly. This repository's pyproject.toml:67 already carries --cov=smoke_optimiser. Recomputing from config therefore lets 'known to the maps' and 'in scope for expiry' drift apart, which is the exact failure this issue names. Recording makes the check unable to disagree with the run that produced the maps, and so-746 already sets the precedent for capture-time facts living in the profile.

WHY TEST PATHS ARE IN SCOPE: tests/*.py are absent from measured_files under --cov=smoke_optimiser and reach knows() only via ImportGraph.unattributed_modules. Scoping to the coverage targets alone would leave a teammate's new tests/test_discounts.py invisible, so the maps would answer confidently and wrongly for an edited rates.py -- so-n6b.1's own motivating scenario, silently under-selected. The cost is accepted: every new test file costs one instrumented full run, which so-n6b.7 prices and so-n6b.17 may reduce.

WHY TRACKED ONLY: an untracked file is one you just created, and so-7hr already places it in the changed set, where so-jr5.2's unknown-changed-path rule answers it and names the accurate reason. Including untracked files in existing_files would give such a file two candidate reasons and buy nothing, since both routes reach a full suite. Tracked-only leaves expiry's domain as files that arrived by pull or checkout -- the only case no other rule sees -- and makes the two domains disjoint by construction. Relying on .gitignore also makes a scope root of '.' survivable, which config.py's _discover_cov_target can produce.

A PROFILE WITH NO RECORDED SCOPE IS A HARD ERROR naming the fix, not a silent full-suite run. This is a 0.x library and a profile is a cache one instrumented run rebuilds, so users reprofile on upgrade rather than being migrated. so-n6b.16 records the schema version that lets the error say what is actually wrong, and blocks so-n6b.1.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER, by decision: a change to the SCOPE ITSELF. Widening --cov makes a whole tree knowable that the maps have never seen, and nothing here expires. That is real, and it is so-n6b.18 rather than part of the MVP, because deciding it requires knowing the scope the NEXT run would measure -- which smoke-optimiser cannot currently determine, for the same reason recomputation was rejected above. A naive 'recorded != currently resolved' comparison is TRUE ON EVERY RUN wherever the project's addopts carry a --cov that differs from what _discover_cov_target returns, pinning the profile to expired forever: the born-expired failure this issue exists to eliminate, reintroduced through the comparison meant to strengthen it. The MVP is therefore tree divergence within a fixed recorded scope, which cannot become permanently expired.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED, do not re-propose:
* Recompute the scope from configuration at check time. Rejected above: cov_source is not the measured scope, the project's addopts are invisible, and the drift is silent.
* Derive the scope from the directory roots of measured_files. Self-consistent, no new field -- but it defines 'in scope' as 'where the profile already has files', which makes the criterion 'a file in scope is one a regenerated profile would know' near-tautological. Under the natural reading (every directory containing a known file) any new subpackage is invisible, and the hole is permanent rather than a one-off cost. It also cannot express scope-drift detection at all, having no recorded scope to compare.
* Filesystem walk instead of git. Needs hand-rolled ignore rules for .venv, __pycache__ and egg-info -- a second definition of 'project file' that drifts from .gitignore.
* Staged files only. Not coherent for an existence question: staging says what is in your commit, not what is on disk and collectable by pytest.

KNOWN HOLE, accepted: source that is gitignored (generated protobuf stubs and the like) never expires a profile. It becomes known once a profiling run measures it.

RECORDED:
* so-n6b.1 -- acceptance criteria rewritten to the scoped comparison, with the scope, the enumerator and the missing-scope error stated.
* so-jr5.2 -- notes carry the scoping of existing_files and the disjointness of the two rules' domains.
* so-jr5.4 -- notes carry the enumeration obligation and the missing-scope error, and state that scope-drift is not its job.
* so-n6b.7 -- criteria widened to split the distribution by test-vs-source, in-vs-out of scope, and tracked-vs-untracked.
* so-n6b.16 -- filed: version the profile file. Blocks so-n6b.1.
* so-n6b.17 -- filed: repair a new-test-file-only expiry by running just those files. Gated on so-n6b.7 and so-jr5.3.
* so-n6b.18 -- filed: scope-drift expiry, including the widening/narrowing asymmetry. Depends on so-n6b.1.

NOT SETTLED HERE: so-n6b.12 asks for the timezone clause to be struck from so-n6b.1's acceptance criteria. The rewritten criteria do not carry it, so n6b.12's acceptance appears met; left open for the epic owner to verify and close.

title: jr5.2's expired-profile blind spot has no input under the signature so-n6b.8 settled
description:
Noticed while settling so-n6b.10, reading jr5.2's blind-spot list against DownwindMaps's actual surface. This is the same failure mode as so-n6b.8 and so-n6b.10, in the one remaining blind spot neither of them touched.

so-jr5.2 lists 'an expired profile (so-n6b.1)' as a blind spot forcing the full suite. so-n6b.8 settled jr5.2's signature as downwind_of(maps, changed_files) -- DownwindMaps and the changed set, nothing else -- and its close reason states that signature 'stays as jr5.1 documented it'.

But so-n6b.1 defines expiry as DIVERGENCE, not age: 'A profile is expired once a file EXISTS that its maps have never seen', with the acceptance criterion 'a file exists in the repository that is absent from both measured_files and the import graph'. Deciding that requires ENUMERATING the files that exist now -- a filesystem or git scan of the whole repo.

Neither input carries it. maps.knows(path) answers per-path and cannot be enumerated over the repo (_known_files is private, and is the profile's file set, not the repo's). changed_files is the diff, not the tree -- a teammate's new billing/discounts.py is precisely a file you did NOT change, which is the exact scenario so-n6b.1's description is built around. So downwind_of as signed today cannot detect the blind spot jr5.2 says it must.

Options:
(a) expiry is decided OUTSIDE downwind_of -- so-jr5.4 (the wiring, which already runs git) computes it and short-circuits to the full-suite path before the rules are consulted. Keeps so-n6b.8's single-input signature intact and keeps DownwindMaps free of IO, but moves one of jr5.2's six named blind spots out of jr5.2, so jr5.2's description and acceptance criteria must stop claiming it.
(b) downwind_of grows a third input (the current repo file set, passed in by the caller so the rules stay pure and IO-free). Keeps all six blind spots in one place, as jr5.2's description argues for ('Splitting them into separately-applied filters invites a rule that quietly wins over another'), but reopens the signature so-n6b.8 just settled.

(b) looks more faithful to jr5.2's own stated reason for being one component, but it reverses a settled decision, so it is a call for the epic owner rather than an implementer. Whichever way it goes changes jr5.2's signature, its tests, and whether so-n6b.1 remains a dependency of jr5.2 or becomes one of so-jr5.4.
acceptance_criteria: jr5.2's expired-profile blind spot has a defined data source, and the owning component is named. If (a), jr5.2's description and acceptance criteria no longer claim the expiry blind spot and the so-n6b.1 dependency edge moves to so-jr5.4. If (b), downwind_of's documented signature is updated and so-n6b.8's close reason is annotated as superseded on that point. Either way, settled before jr5.2 is implemented.
close_reason:
Settled as option (b) by the epic owner. The expired-profile blind spot STAYS in so-jr5.2, and downwind_of grows a third input:

  downwind_of(maps, changed_files, existing_files) -> DownwindResult

existing_files is the set of files that exist in the working tree now, enumerated by so-jr5.4 and passed in as plain data, so the rules stay pure and IO-free and DownwindMaps stays free of the filesystem. Expiry is 'any(not maps.knows(p) for p in existing_files)' -- so-n6b.1's divergence definition read straight off the maps' public surface.

DECIDING REASON: expiry and the unknown-changed-path rule overlap. A file you add yourself is both a changed path the maps have never seen and the file that expires the profile -- one answer, two candidate reasons, and per so-jr5.4 the reason is the whole product when the tool declines to select. Under option (a) the short-circuit in jr5.4 would always win, the unknown-path rule could never fire in that case, and jr5.2's unit tests would keep passing because they exercise downwind_of in isolation and never see the short-circuit above them. That is exactly the 'rule that quietly wins over another' jr5.2's description exists to prevent, made harder to catch by crossing a component boundary no single test observes. It also keeps expiry consistent with resolution_errors, already a whole-profile blind spot that so-n6b.8 deliberately placed inside jr5.2 rather than in the caller.

The cost was real and accepted: it reverses so-n6b.8 on the signature, and existing_files is the one input not derived from the profile, carrying a scoping policy likely to churn (so-746, monorepo roots).

RECORDED:
• so-jr5.2 -- notes carry the settled signature and the rule-ordering obligation; acceptance criteria now require the expiry refusal and the expiry/unknown-path interaction test.
• so-n6b.8 -- annotated SUPERSEDED IN PART: its single-input signature statement no longer holds, its substantive finding stands.
• so-jr5.4 -- noted that it must enumerate existing_files (the tree, not so-7hr's diff).
• so-n6b.1 stays a dependency of so-jr5.2. It did not move.

NOT settled here, by decision: what scopes existing_files. so-n6b.1's literal criterion matches README.md and would expire every profile always; that is now so-n6b.14, blocking so-n6b.1.

title: jr5.2's acceptance criteria contradict its own description on failed-importer tests
description:
Noticed while settling so-n6b.8, which read jr5.2's description and acceptance criteria side by side.

so-jr5.2's DESCRIPTION lists, as a blind spot forcing the full suite: 'an import graph with any non-zero resolution_errors ... until so-n6b.2 localises the doubt by importer, the whole graph is treated as untrustworthy.'

Its ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA say: 'Failed-importer tests are added to an otherwise ordinary answer.'

These cannot both hold. Adding failed-importer tests to an ordinary answer IS so-n6b.2's localised rule (bd show so-n6b.2: 'selection ALWAYS additionally runs every test whose closure reaches a module in failed_importers'), and it presupposes failed_importers, which so-n6b.5 has not yet recorded -- ImportGraph today carries only a resolution_errors count and repr() error_samples, with no importer attached.

Whichever way it is settled changes what jr5.2 must implement and what its tests assert, so it should be settled before jr5.2 starts rather than discovered mid-implementation -- the same failure mode so-n6b.8 was filed for.

Options:
(a) the acceptance criterion is a leak from so-n6b.2 and should be struck from jr5.2, leaving the blunt full-suite refusal that jr5.2's own description and so-n6b.2's existence both assume;
(b) jr5.2 is genuinely meant to carry the localised rule, in which case it depends on so-n6b.5 and so-n6b.2 rather than being replaced by them, and the dependency edges need reversing.

(a) looks right, but it is a call for the epic owner, not an implementer.
close_reason: Settled as option (a): the criterion 'Failed-importer tests are added to an otherwise ordinary answer' was a leak from so-n6b.2 and has been struck from so-jr5.2. jr5.2 ships the blunt whole-graph refusal on any non-zero resolution_errors, as its own description states; so-n6b.2 (depending on so-n6b.5 for failed_importers) later replaces that refusal with the localised always-run set. Existing dependency edges are correct and unchanged. Verified against the code: failed_importers exists nowhere in the repo, so jr5.2 could not have implemented the localised rule today.

title: DownwindMaps doesn't expose unattributed_modules or resolution_errors, but jr5.2's blind-spot rules need both
description:
so-jr5.1 (DownwindMaps.from_profile) is documented as the sole input to jr5.2's rules -- its own design note gives the consumer signature as downwind_of(maps, changed_files), taking only the DownwindMaps object, not the raw ProfilingData or ImportGraph.

But so-jr5.2's blind spots explicitly require two pieces of ImportGraph that DownwindMaps (smoke_optimiser/downwind/maps.py) currently has no accessor for:

* 'a changed file in ImportGraph.unattributed_modules' -- DownwindMaps.knows(path) folds unattributed_modules into known_files (by design, so a conftest.py or test module counts as known), which means a caller cannot currently tell 'known and attributed' apart from 'known only because it is unattributed'. There is no unattributed(path) query.
* 'an import graph with any non-zero resolution_errors' -- DownwindMaps stores no resolution_errors count at all; it is dropped during from_profile.

Either DownwindMaps needs two more accessors (e.g. is_unattributed(path) -> bool and has_resolution_errors -> bool / resolution_errors -> int), or downwind_of's signature needs to take the ImportGraph/ProfilingData alongside maps. This is a design call -- whichever way it goes affects both DownwindMaps's public surface and jr5.2's function signature, so it should be settled before jr5.2 is implemented rather than discovered mid-implementation.
acceptance_criteria: DownwindMaps (or its caller's signature) provides everything jr5.2 needs to detect both blind spots without reaching back into raw ProfilingData/ImportGraph via a side channel. Covered by a test asserting a changed unattributed file and a changed file under a degraded graph are each still distinguishable via DownwindMaps's public surface (or the agreed alternative).
notes:
SUPERSEDED IN PART by so-n6b.11 (settled 2026-09-07). This issue's close reason states that downwind_of keeps its single-input signature, downwind_of(maps, changed_files). That no longer holds: so-n6b.11 settled the expired-profile blind spot as option (b), giving downwind_of a third input --

  downwind_of(maps, changed_files, existing_files)

-- because so-n6b.1 defines expiry as divergence, which requires enumerating the files that exist NOW, and neither of the two original inputs carries that.

Everything else here stands. The substantive finding -- that jr5.2's two graph blind spots are read off DownwindMaps's own surface via is_unattributed(path) and resolution_errors, rather than by handing the rules the raw ImportGraph/ProfilingData -- is unchanged and is what DownwindMaps implements today.
close_reason: DownwindMaps now carries both facts: is_unattributed(path) -> bool (raises UnknownFileError like the other lookups) and resolution_errors -> int. downwind_of(maps, changed_files) stays as jr5.1 documented it.

title: Wire up the downwind command, from git diff to pytest invocation
description:
`smoke-optimiser downwind`, the user-facing command: read the profile, collect the
changed set, apply the downwind rules, write the selection file, and run pytest --
either the tests downwind of the change, or the full suite when the answer is a
refusal.

Wiring only. Every decision it acts on belongs to a sibling issue; this is where they
meet, plus the surface a precommit hook actually calls. Completing it is the point at
which the feature exists end to end and can start shaking out bugs against real
edits.

  - A command distinct from the coverage-per-second path, which keeps its behaviour
    unchanged.
  - Configuration through pyproject.toml as well as flags, on the precedence rules
    so-qex establishes.
  - Reporting: which files were considered changed, how many tests were selected out
    of how many, and -- when it refused -- which blind spot caused it. The
    reason is the whole product when the tool declines to select, so it is not a
    debug-level detail.
  - Exit code reflects pytest's, on the exit-code handling so-2os establishes, so a
    failing selected test fails the commit and a collection error never passes as a
    successful selective run.

Both of those prerequisites are load-bearing rather than incidental: a command that
gates a commit is worthless if a collection error reads as success, and a
configuration surface that silently ignores pyproject.toml would make the rules
behave differently from how the project asked.

REFUSES TO RUN OUTSIDE THE REPOSITORY ROOT. git reports repo-relative paths and the
profile's paths are relative to the invocation directory, so the two agree only when
those coincide. Rather than assume it, require it: erroring is loud, whereas a
mismatch selects nothing for a file plenty of tests depend on and looks perfectly
healthy doing it. so-746 removes the restriction by making the profile's paths
repo-relative outright, which is what a monorepo needs.

FALLS BACK BY RUNNING PLAIN PYTEST, and printing the command to regenerate the
profile. so-jr5.3 later makes that fallback instrumented so it rewrites the profile
it fell back from; until then staleness is corrected by hand.

An end-to-end test over a fixture project: edit a file, assert the selected node
ids; edit a file the maps have never seen, assert the full suite ran and the blind
spot was reported.
acceptance_criteria: Running the command in a fixture project with one edited source file runs exactly the tests the map attributes to it. With an edited file the maps have never seen it runs the whole suite and names the blind spot. A failing selected test yields a non-zero exit code, and a collection error never reads as success. Invoked from a subdirectory it errors rather than selecting. The coverage-per-second command's behaviour is unchanged.
notes:
so-n6b.11 settled: this command must ENUMERATE the files that exist in the working tree and pass them to the rules as downwind_of's third argument, existing_files. so-jr5.2 owns the expiry rule and reads it off that set; jr5.4 owns getting it, since it is the component that already touches git and the filesystem. This is enumeration, not a decision -- consistent with 'wiring only'. It is a different query from so-7hr's changed set: the tree, not the diff, and gathered separately.

WHICH FILES belong in the set is settled by so-n6b.14; jr5.4 applies that scope rather than inventing one. existing_files is 'git ls-files' -- tracked only, no --others -- filtered to .py, restricted to the scope roots the profile recorded at capture time. Tracked only because an untracked file is one you just created, which so-7hr already places in the changed set, where jr5.2's unknown-path rule answers it with the more accurate reason. Relying on .gitignore for exclusion is also what makes a scope root of '.' survivable at all: config.py's _discover_cov_target falls back to '.' for a project with no src/ and no name-matching package, and a filesystem walk would then need hand-rolled ignore rules for .venv and friends -- a second, drifting definition of what counts as a project file.

A profile with no recorded scope is a hard error naming the fix, not a silent full-suite run.

jr5.4 does NOT compare the recorded scope against the current configuration. Detecting that the scope itself has changed is so-n6b.18, and it is a harder problem than a set comparison: the effective scope of the next run is not currently knowable ahead of the run, so a naive comparison can be permanently true and pin the tool to the full-suite path forever.

title: Run the full-suite fallback under instrumentation, so it rewrites the profile it fell back from
description:
A full-suite fallback runs under profiling instrumentation and rewrites the profile.
The run that pays for the fallback is the run that repairs the map.

Without this, staleness is a ratchet: the map expires, every commit pays a full
suite, and it keeps paying until a human remembers to run smoke-optimiser by hand.
With it, a fallback costs one instrumented full run -- measured at +11% on
enphase_curtailer, 61s -> 68s -- and the next commit selects a subset again.

It also settles what "regenerate" means without a background process. Nothing
detaches, nothing fires at an unpredictable moment, and nothing runs that the
developer did not already have to wait for.

REQUIRES the fallback to run through our own entry point rather than the tool merely
telling a caller to run everything. That is a constraint on the execution path
(so-uom), not an afterthought.

MUST NOT OVERWRITE A GOOD PROFILE WITH A PARTIAL ONE. pytest_unconfigure does not
run when the process is hard-killed -- timeout, OOM, SIGKILL -- and under xdist a
single killed worker means one missing per-worker file that merges silently into a
graph that looks complete (so-my1, and so-fp4 for the same class in the coverage
database). The rewrite must be atomic and conditional: a run that did not produce
complete data leaves the previous profile in place, and says so.

A fallback whose tests FAIL still produces a valid map -- ProfilingOutcome already
records passed -- so the rewrite is conditioned on the data being complete, not on
the suite being green.
acceptance_criteria: A run that falls back to the full suite leaves a profile behind, so an immediately repeated run selects a subset. A fallback with failing tests still rewrites the profile. A fallback killed part-way leaves the previous profile intact and reports that it did not regenerate. Under xdist, a missing worker's data prevents the rewrite rather than producing a thinner map.
notes: Replaces the stand-in so-jr5.4 ships with, where a full-suite fallback runs plain pytest and prints the command to regenerate the profile by hand. That stand-in is correct but makes staleness a ratchet: every commit pays a full suite until someone remembers to regenerate.

title: The downwind rules: answer from the maps, or refuse and name the blind spot
description:
The downwind rules: given the changed set and the downwind maps, produce either the
tests downwind of that change or a refusal naming the blind spot it could not answer
for. Everything else
in this line of work feeds it or carries its answer.

It is one component because the rules are not independent. A changed file can be
answerable by coverage and unanswerable by the graph at the same time; a conftest.py
is both a Python file with a directory rule and a module the graph may have edges
for; a degraded graph adds selections regardless of what changed. Splitting them
into separately-applied filters invites a rule that quietly wins over another.

DOWNWIND, for a changed Python file the maps know: the union of the tests that
executed it and the tests whose modules transitively import it.

BLIND SPOTS, each meaning the full suite with the offending input named:
  - a changed path with no entry in the map -- new code, exactly when tests matter
    most;
  - a changed path that is not Python. The map is a Python-execution map, so absence
    tells us nothing about a data file (so-n6b.4 makes these answerable for real);
  - a changed file in ImportGraph.unattributed_modules, where the graph is blind to
    who depends on it. Reading that as "nothing imports this" selects zero tests,
    which is the silent under-selection this design exists to prevent;
  - an expired profile (so-n6b.1);
  - a changed conftest.py. Blunt but sound: a conftest's fixtures leave no
    distinguishing mark in the map, so nothing here can tell which tests used them.
    so-017 narrows this to pytest's own directory scope afterwards;
  - an import graph with any non-zero resolution_errors. Also blunt, and deliberately
    the safe direction: a swallowed failure is a missing edge and the count alone
    cannot say which, so until so-n6b.2 localises the doubt by importer, the whole
    graph is treated as untrustworthy.

Both blunt rules over-select, never under-select, so narrowing them later is a
refinement rather than a correction. Neither may be relaxed without the issue that
replaces it.

The result is a typed value carrying the node ids or the refusal AND its reason --
never a bare list, and never a list that silently happens to be everything. Blind
spots travel on it as blind_spots, keeping the epic's vocabulary rather than
degrading to "unknown" at the boundary. A caller
must be unable to confuse "these 37 tests are the answer" with "I could not answer,
so here is everything".

Refusal reasons are values, not strings: the reason is written into the selection
file, reported to the user, and tested against.
acceptance_criteria: Each blind spot independently produces a refusal carrying its own reason. A changed file answerable by coverage but unattributed in the graph refuses rather than answering partially. A changed file under a graph with any non-zero resolution_errors refuses, naming the count, regardless of what else the maps could say about it. A file that EXISTS but is absent from the maps refuses with expiry as the reason, even when every changed file is known. A refusal is structurally distinct from a selection listing every test. Covered by unit tests over hand-built profiles, one per rule and one per interaction between rules -- including the case where a newly added file is BOTH a changed path the maps have never seen and the file that expires the profile, which must report a single, defined reason.
notes:
so-n6b.8 is settled: the two graph blind spots are read off DownwindMaps, not off ImportGraph. downwind_of(maps, changed_files) keeps its single-input signature.

- 'a changed file in ImportGraph.unattributed_modules' is now maps.is_unattributed(path) -> bool
- 'non-zero resolution_errors' is now maps.resolution_errors -> int (the count, so the refusal reason can say how incomplete the graph is; error_samples stay in the profile JSON)

Rule ORDER matters: is_unattributed, tests_executing and dependents_of all raise UnknownFileError for a path the maps have never seen, so the unknown-path blind spot must be checked (via maps.knows) before any of them is called.

so-n6b.10 is settled: the acceptance criterion 'Failed-importer tests are added to an otherwise ordinary answer' was a leak from so-n6b.2 and has been struck. jr5.2 implements the BLUNT rule its own description states -- any non-zero resolution_errors refuses the whole graph and names the count. It does not add failed-importer tests, and must not: failed_importers does not exist yet (so-n6b.5 records it) and there is nothing on DownwindMaps to read it from.

The dependency edges are correct as they stand: so-n6b.2 depends on so-jr5.2 and so-n6b.5, and REPLACES jr5.2's blunt refusal with the localised always-run set. Per jr5.2's own description the blunt rule 'may not be relaxed without the issue that replaces it', and so-n6b.2 is that issue.
so-n6b.11 is settled, option (b): the expired-profile blind spot STAYS in jr5.2, and downwind_of grows a third input.

  downwind_of(maps, changed_files, existing_files) -> DownwindResult

existing_files is the set of files that exist in the working tree now, enumerated and scoped by the CALLER (so-jr5.4, which already runs git) and passed in as plain data. The rules stay pure and IO-free: jr5.2 never touches the filesystem or git. Expiry is then 'any(not maps.knows(p) for p in existing_files)' -- so-n6b.1's divergence definition, read straight off the maps' public surface.

This SUPERSEDES so-n6b.8's close reason on the signature point only. so-n6b.8's substantive finding stands unchanged: the two graph blind spots are read off DownwindMaps via is_unattributed(path) and resolution_errors, not off raw ImportGraph. What no longer holds is its statement that downwind_of keeps a single-input signature.

WHY (b) rather than deciding expiry outside jr5.2: expiry and the unknown-changed-path rule OVERLAP. A file you add yourself is both a changed path the maps have never seen and the file that expires the profile -- one answer, two candidate reasons, and the reason is the product. Deciding expiry in jr5.4 ahead of the rules means the unknown-path rule can never fire in that case, while jr5.2's unit tests keep passing because they exercise downwind_of in isolation and never see the short-circuit above them. That is precisely the 'rule that quietly wins over another' this issue's description exists to prevent, made worse by crossing a component boundary no single test observes. It is also consistent with resolution_errors, already a whole-profile blind spot that so-n6b.8 deliberately placed inside jr5.2 rather than in the caller.

Rule ORDER now covers three interacting cases, all decided here and all tested: maps.knows before is_unattributed/tests_executing/dependents_of (they raise UnknownFileError); and expiry against the unknown-changed-path rule, whose precedence must be an explicit, visible line rather than an accident of ordering.

WHAT SCOPES existing_files is NOT settled here -- see the issue blocking so-n6b.1. jr5.2 takes the set it is given; the policy deciding which files belong in it is the caller's and so-n6b.1's.
EXISTING_FILES, the third input, is scoped by so-n6b.14: .py files under the scope roots the profile recorded at capture time, tracked by git. so-jr5.4 enumerates and scopes them; jr5.2 receives the set and never asks where it came from.

That scoping makes the expiry and unknown-changed-path rules DISJOINT in practice as well as in principle. existing_files holds tracked files only, so a file you created yourself is untracked, absent from existing_files, and reaches the rules solely through changed_files -- where the unknown-path rule answers it and names it accurately. Expiry then fires only for files that arrived by pull or checkout, which is the case no other rule sees. The rule-ordering obligation stands regardless: expiry must not be allowed to pre-empt a reason the unknown-path rule would give better, and a test must pin which reason a file reachable by both routes receives.

title: Build the downwind maps: invert the profile into file -> tests and file -> dependents
description:
The profile stores the relation test -> files. Selection needs it the other way
round, and needs it fast enough to answer per changed file without rescanning
thousands of test records each time.

Build, from a loaded ProfilingData:
  - file -> tests that executed it, inverted from every ProfilingOutcome's
    files_covered;
  - file -> files that import it, inverted from ImportGraph.edges, with the
    transitive closure available so a changed file yields every module that
    depends on it however many hops away;
  - the set of files the profile knows about at all, from measured_files unioned
    with every path appearing in the graph, since "no entry" and "not known" must
    be distinguishable by the rules that consume this.

Pure functions over the loaded profile, no IO and no git. That is the point: the
arithmetic here is where an off-by-one in a closure quietly loses tests, and it
should be testable with a hand-built ProfilingData rather than an end-to-end run.

Closure computation must handle import cycles without recursing forever -- Python
allows them and real projects have them.
design:
DOWNWIND MAPS are the data structure the whole feature reads from: given a changed
file, what is downwind of it. This issue builds them; so-jr5.2 applies the rules that
consume them. The naming and the shared vocabulary, blind_spots included, are settled
on so-n6b.

MODULE LAYOUT for the downwind-mvp set:

  smoke_optimiser/downwind/__init__.py
  smoke_optimiser/downwind/maps.py      this issue
  smoke_optimiser/downwind/rules.py     so-jr5.2
  smoke_optimiser/downwind/changes.py   so-7hr, git diff -> changed set
  smoke_optimiser/reports/downwind_selection.py   so-uom

SURFACE this issue owns:

  maps = DownwindMaps.from_profile(profiling_data)
  maps.tests_executing(path)   inverted files_covered
  maps.dependents_of(path)     transitive closure of ImportGraph.edges
  maps.knows(path)             measured_files unioned with graph paths

so-jr5.2 consumes it as downwind_of(maps, changed_files), returning the selected
tests, the blind spots and the reason.
acceptance_criteria: A file executed by three tests maps to exactly those three. A file imported by a module that a test module imports appears in that test's dependency closure. A cycle A->B->A terminates and yields both. A file present in measured_files but executed by no test is known-with-no-tests, distinct from a file the maps do not know at all. Built once per profile, not per changed file.
close_reason: DownwindMaps.from_profile implemented in smoke_optimiser/downwind/maps.py, 7 tests covering every acceptance criterion, 100% coverage on the module, committed as e2b6820

title: Run what's downwind: select the tests a change can reach, end to end
description:
smoke-optimiser's existing smoke mode selects a STATIC subset -- highest coverage
per second, the same tests whatever you changed. That is a coverage bet: it cannot
promise the coverage it skips, so it cannot gate a commit.

This is the second, honest selection mode: DOWNWIND. Given the files changed in the
working tree, run every test that is downwind of them -- every test the profile says
those changes can reach -- and run the full suite wherever the maps cannot answer. The promise is categorical and literally statable,
which is the whole point: every test that has ever executed a line you touched,
plus every test that transitively imports a file you touched.

WHY IT IS POSSIBLE. The profiling data already IS a test-impact map.
ProfilingOutcome.files_covered gives file -> tests directly, and ImportGraph.edges
gives the dependency relation that answers for a file which only ever runs at
import time -- a constants module, a Pydantic model, a package re-export -- which
coverage records under no test context at all.

MEASURED on enphase_curtailer: 2600 tests, 190 files in the map, MEDIAN 37 TESTS
PER FILE. Touch one source file and you run ~37 of 2600. The full suite is 55s
warm on a 10-core Mac and 7m32s on GitHub CI's 4 cores.

GRANULARITY: FILE-LEVEL. Deliberately not line-level. Line numbers shift the moment
you insert a line above, so a line-level map silently mismatches after almost any
edit. File-level is immune to line shifts, reformatting and refactors within a
file. so-aif is the deferred line-level follow-up.

THE MAPS MUST NEVER GUESS. Every input is either answered from recorded fact or
declared a blind spot, and a blind spot means the full suite with a stated reason.
There is no best-effort middle: the moment it selects a subset it cannot justify it
is test-fast again and cannot gate a commit.

SELF-HEALING. A full-suite fallback runs under profiling instrumentation and
rewrites the profile, so the run that pays for the fallback is also the run that
repairs the map. Instrumentation costs +11% (measured on enphase: 61s -> 68s), and
it means staleness costs one full run rather than accumulating until someone
remembers to regenerate by hand. Nothing regenerates in the background, and no
regeneration the developer did not ask for ever blocks a commit.

DOES NOT COVER, and must not pretend to: npm/vitest suites, tsc typechecks, codegen
drift checks, Rust. In casey_ai the heavy precommit item is a Docker integration
suite; only the Python half is in scope here.

This epic is the shared spec. Its children carry the work.
design:
THE INPUT is the union of staged, unstaged and untracked changes, because pytest
reads the worktree rather than the index: selecting on the index alone would test
something other than what is about to run. Renames are detected (-M) and resolved
to the OLD path, the only path the profile knows. A deleted file is looked up in
the map exactly like any other change -- the tests that executed it are the ones
most likely to break -- so nothing may gate on whether a path still exists on disk.

PATHS ARE REPO-RELATIVE throughout, from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, so the
profile and git agree by construction rather than by coincidence of the directory
smoke-optimiser was invoked from.

DOWNWIND OF a changed file is the union of:
  - tests whose files_covered contains it (it executed under that test), and
  - tests whose module transitively imports it, via the inverted ImportGraph.

BLIND SPOTS -- run the full suite, and say which input caused it:
  - a changed path with no entry in the map (new code, which is exactly when tests
    matter most);
  - a changed path that is not Python at all (YAML, templates, assets, lockfiles,
    workflows). The map is a Python-execution map, so absence carries no
    information about a data file: it means "we never looked", not "nothing reads
    this". so-n6b.4 makes these answerable for real;
  - a changed file listed in ImportGraph.unattributed_modules, which means the
    graph is blind to who depends on it;
  - a profile whose map has never seen a file that exists now (see EXPIRY);
  - an import graph carrying failures we could not localise (see TRUST).

A CHANGED conftest.py selects every test at or below its directory, mirroring
pytest's own scoping rule, so a root conftest.py selects the whole suite and a
leaf one does not. A changed test file selects the tests in that file; a test file
that other tests import from is covered by the import graph like any other module.

EXPIRY is divergence, not age. A profile is expired once a file exists that its map
has never seen, because from that moment the map can answer confidently and wrongly:
the tests added since capture are absent from every answer it gives. Divergence is
a cliff rather than a slope, and the self-healing fallback is what makes the cliff
affordable -- hitting it costs one instrumented full run, not a full run on every
commit until someone regenerates by hand.

TRUST. The import tracer swallows and counts edge-resolution failures, because
raising inside __import__ would kill the suite being profiled. Every such failure
is our defect, not the project's -- it is our name arithmetic failing on legal
Python -- so the user must not be made to pay a full suite for it. The failure loses
the IMPORTED name while the IMPORTER is still in hand, so the doubt localises to
the importer: selection always additionally runs every test whose closure reaches a
module with a failed edge. Failures where even the importer could not be recovered
are counted separately and do force the full suite, since there is nothing to
localise them to.

NAMING is settled, and the vocabulary is shared by every child issue. The mode is
DOWNWIND: given a change, the tests downwind of it. The metaphor is the product's
own -- smoke goes somewhere, and what is downwind of the source gets it -- so
`--smoke` and `--downwind` sit beside each other without either needing a glossary.
It is neutral about the change, which matters: a code change is expected work, not
an incident, and a name implying fault would be wrong every time it was read.

BLIND SPOTS is the name, in every layer, for inputs the maps cannot answer for --
the ones that force the full suite. The field is blind_spots and the concept keeps
that name from the maps through the rules, the selection file, and the console
output the developer reads when the tool declines to select. Not "unknown", not
"unanswerable", in code.

OUTPUT is its own file with its own schema and its own pytest flag: `pytest
--downwind` reads `.downwind.json`, beside the existing `--smoke` and
`.smoke_suite.json`. The categorical promise has no time cap, no coverage target and
no efficiency ranking, so it shares nothing with SmokeSuiteFile but the list of node
ids.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED, and rejected -- do not re-propose without new evidence:

  - Naming the mode anything other than downwind. Rejected, with the reason each
    one fails, so none of them comes back:
      touched, affected, impact  -- the tests are not the affected party; the code
        is. "Affected tests" also reads as a status the tests acquired rather than
        a selection made about them.
      blast (radius), cascade, tripwire, resonance -- all carry fault or incident.
        A change is expected work. Cascade additionally inverts on the fire
        metaphor, since its literal sense is a waterfall.
      cone (of influence), reach, span, hull, orbit -- correct terms of art, but
        each needs explaining at the CLI, where `--downwind` explains itself.
      guard, detector -- accurate about the relationship, but they open a second
        metaphor beside the smoke already in the product's name.
      spanner -- a real graph-theory object and a genuine pun, lost to three
        collisions: the database, the wrench, and "a spanner in the works".
  - Staged-only input (--cached). Rejected: pytest runs against the worktree, so an
    unstaged edit changes what the selected tests execute.
  - Treating a rename's new path as unknown, or forgoing -M so it appears as an
    add plus a delete. Both make every pure move cost a full suite.
  - A user-configurable ignore list for non-Python paths, so a README edit does not
    cost a full run. Rejected: "this path is irrelevant" is a claim that should be
    MEASURED, not asserted -- an asserted list is silent under-selection the moment
    it is wrong. so-n6b.3 measures it instead.
  - Wall-clock expiry with a configured threshold. Rejected: it is a heuristic that
    reads a day of heavy refactoring as fresh and an untouched fortnight as stale,
    while divergence measures the thing that actually breaks the map.
  - Refusing any profile with non-zero resolution_errors. Rejected: it punishes the
    user durably for our bug, since the failures are deterministic and persist
    until we fix the tracer.
  - Trusting a degraded graph with only a warning. Rejected: that is the silent
    under-selection this whole line of work exists to prevent.
  - Printing node ids for the caller to pass to pytest, with no file. Rejected: it
    puts a full suite's worth of argv on the command line at 2600 tests, and the
    fallback must run through our entry point for the self-healing rewrite to
    happen at all.
  - Regenerating the profile in a detached background process. Rejected: a full
    suite firing at an unpredictable moment is worse than the instrumented
    fallback, which pays the cost exactly when the developer was already paying it.
acceptance_criteria: Changing a source file runs exactly the tests that executed it plus the tests whose modules transitively import it, and no others. Changing a file absent from the map, a non-Python file, an unattributed module, or a file in a repository whose map has never seen some existing file, runs the full suite and names the blind spot that caused it. Changing tests/sub/conftest.py runs every test under tests/sub/ and nothing outside it. A deleted file still selects the tests that executed it. A full-suite fallback rewrites the profile, so an immediately repeated run selects a subset instead of falling back again.
notes:
WHAT THE PROFILE PROVIDES, and what each part is for:

  - ProfilingOutcome.files_covered: every measured file a test executed, branchless
    files included, so a straight-line constants module is visible where
    branches_covered cannot see it.
  - ProfilingData.measured_files: everything coverage measured, executed or not, so
    "coverage never saw this file" is distinguishable from "no test ran it".
  - ImportGraph.edges: (importer, imported) as project-relative paths. Invert and
    take the transitive closure for every test module depending on a changed file.
  - ImportGraph.unattributed_modules: project files loaded that nothing was seen to
    import -- test modules, conftest.py, and any pytest11 plugin belonging to the
    project, since pytest loads entry-point plugins before any hook can watch. A
    change to one means the graph CANNOT ANSWER.
  - ImportGraph.resolution_errors / error_samples / failed_importers: edge recording
    that failed and was swallowed, because raising inside __import__ would kill the
    run being profiled.

Measured on smoke-optimiser itself: 91 edges, 17 unattributed of ~35 project files.

WHAT AN IMPORT CLOSURE SELECTS, as a percentage of the suite, per source file, from
a --collect-only prototype (2026-09-06):

  repo                tests  files   p25    median   p75    max     mean
  smoke-optimiser        81     19  18.5%   27.2%   48.1%  87.7%   33.3%
  casey_ai/api         1389    143  20.5%   47.7%   52.1%  96.5%   39.4%
  enphase_curtailer    2600    271   7.3%   12.8%   21.9%  93.2%   17.5%

The decisive case is casey_ai: db/models/common.py reaches 96.5% of the suite
(genuinely global -- running everything IS right), while db/models/interval.py and
db/models/task.py reach 3 tests each. Same directory, same kind of declaration file.
The graph tells them apart; a file-glob heuristic cannot.

CAVEAT: measured with --collect-only, so it misses imports made lazily inside test
bodies. Real closures may be marginally wider.
MVP, labelled downwind-mvp: so-jr5.1, so-jr5.2, so-7hr, so-uom, so-jr5.4,
so-n6b.1, plus so-2os and so-qex. That is the whole path from a git diff to a pytest
run, with expiry included so the answer is trustworthy rather than merely fast.

It ships with three conservative stand-ins, each of which over-selects or errors
rather than under-selecting, and each of which is replaced by a named issue:

  - any changed conftest.py is a blind spot      -> so-017
  - any non-zero resolution_errors distrusts the graph -> so-n6b.2
  - the fallback runs plain pytest, regenerate by hand -> so-jr5.3
  - the command refuses to run outside the repository root -> so-746

Sequenced this way so the feature exists end to end early and gets exercised against
real edits, rather than being assembled correct-on-paper and met all at once.

title: Capture the real import graph during profiling, so a change to an import-only module selects its importers instead of the whole suite
description:
so-d8v gave the profile per-test files_covered and top-level measured_files. That fixes the REASONING for a changed file no test executes at runtime, but not the SELECTION: a Pydantic model or constants module that only ever runs at import time still forces a full-suite run, because coverage records import-time execution under the empty context and never records WHO imported it.

The missing relation is the import graph. With it, a changed import-only module selects the tests whose modules transitively import it, which measurement shows is a 60-83% saving over running everything (see NOTES).

Scope of this issue is CAPTURE ONLY -- record the graph into the profile. Consuming it for selection is so-jr5.
acceptance_criteria: A profile recorded from a suite where module A imports module B, and module C also imports B with A collected first, contains BOTH the A->B and C->B edges. A module imported only at collection time (never executed under any test context) still has its importers recorded. Edges resolve to project-relative file paths; site-packages and .venv are excluded.
notes:
MEASUREMENT THAT JUSTIFIES THIS (2026-09-06). Percentage of the suite an import
closure selects, computed per source file, via a --collect-only prototype:

repo                tests  files   p25    median   p75    max     mean
smoke-optimiser        81     19  18.5%   27.2%   48.1%  87.7%   33.3%
casey_ai/api         1389    143  20.5%   47.7%   52.1%  96.5%   39.4%
enphase_curtailer    2600    271   7.3%   12.8%   21.9%  93.2%   17.5%

Against the current 100% fallback that is a 60-83% saving on exactly the edits
that trigger a full run today.

The decisive case is casey_ai: db/models/common.py reaches 96.5% of the suite
(genuinely global, running everything IS right), while db/models/interval.py and
db/models/task.py reach 3 tests each (0.2%) -- same directory, same kind of
declaration file, not re-exported through the package __init__. Today all three
are treated identically. The graph gets both right.

CAVEAT ON THE NUMBERS: measured with --collect-only, which misses imports made
lazily inside test function bodies, so real closures may be marginally wider.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

DECISIONS 2026-09-06 (user, answering the open questions in DESIGN):

1. ERROR POLICY: swallow-and-count. Edge recording catches, increments a counter
and keeps the first N exception reprs; both land in the profile so a degraded
graph is visible to so-jr5 rather than silently under-selecting. Costs one
documented noqa BLE001, matching the precedent in smoke_optimiser/plugin.py.

2. CODE LOCATION: a real typed module, smoke_optimiser/profiler/import_tracer.py,
imported normally. NOT the PYTEST_HOOK_CODE inline string. Decisive fact:
pyproject.toml already registers smoke_optimiser.plugin as a pytest11 entry
point, and the runner invokes sys.executable -m pytest, so smoke_optimiser is
ALREADY imported into every profiled run -- the dependency-free-subprocess
argument for the inline string is void. The win is unit-testability of the
edge-resolution arithmetic (level>1 relative imports becomes a 3-line test
rather than a nested fixture project run end to end), which matters because the
bug class here is a MISSING edge: it raises nothing and is invisible to an e2e
test.

3. MECHANISMS: implement BOTH the builtins.__import__ wrapper and the
sys.meta_path finder for importlib.import_module first-loads, in this issue.

4. XDIST: fix so-u3i FIRST, then implement edge capture consistently with the
write/merge path it establishes. so-u3i is now decided: support xdist, per-worker
files merged by the runner, runtime detection (not arg sniffing), worker count
recorded in the profile, and the TIME-based optimiser errors on a parallel
profile while map-only consumers stay silent.

IMPLEMENTATION DECISIONS 2026-09-06 (user), on top of the four already recorded:

5. THREE MECHANISMS, not two:
   - builtins.__import__ wrapper: every execution of an import statement, importer
     from globals["__name__"]. Primary.
   - importlib.import_module wrapper: import_module bypasses builtins.__import__
     entirely. Importer comes from the CALLER FRAME (sys._getframe), which is
     unambiguous at the call site, and it fires on every call rather than only on
     first load. Chosen over stack-walking inside find_spec, which would have to
     skip a variable number of importlib bootstrap frames and misattributes when
     the import happens inside a helper in another module.
   - sys.meta_path finder: the wider net for first loads through entry points
     neither wrapper sees (importlib.util, pkgutil, C-level __import__).

6. THE FINDER RECORDS LOADS, NOT EDGES. find_spec receives no globals, so it
   cannot know the importer, and NO frame heuristic is used to guess one. It
   records the module name only. At snapshot time any PROJECT module that was
   loaded but has zero importer edges is reported as unattributed_modules.
   so-jr5 must treat a change to one of those files as "cannot answer" -> run the
   full suite, NOT as "nothing imports it" -> select nothing. A wrong edge
   over-selects quietly; a missing edge under-selects silently, which is the exact
   failure this issue exists to prevent, so the blind spot is made loud instead of
   guessed at.

7. INSTALLED FROM THE PROFILING HOOK (_smoke_hook, passed with -p by the runner),
   not from the shipped smoke_optimiser/plugin.py. plugin.py is loaded by the
   pytest11 entry point into EVERY pytest run of every project that installs
   smoke-optimiser, so installing there would need an env-var gate to stay inert;
   the profiling-only plugin needs no gate and keeps profiling concerns out of the
   --smoke filter. Both are loaded at pytest startup, so both are early enough to
   precede collection.

8. XDIST: follows the path so-u3i established -- one graph file per worker,
   suffixed by PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER, unioned by the runner. Edges are a set, so the
   merge is a plain union; error and load counts sum.

title: Files with no branches never appear in the coverage map, so change-based selection cannot see them
description:
ProfilingOutcome.branches_covered holds branch ids only. so-jr5 plans to invert
that map to get file -> tests, but a source file containing NO BRANCHES produces
no branch ids at all, so it is absent from the map entirely.

Straight-line code is common and exactly the kind that has no branches:
constants modules, __init__.py re-export files, dataclass and Pydantic model
definitions, thin delegating wrappers, protocol/ABC declarations. In this
repository smoke_optimiser/profiler/models.py and optimiser/models.py are both
pure declaration files.

CONSEQUENCE FOR so-jr5. Its fallback rule is 'a file with no entry in the map
means new code, so run everything'. A branchless file hits that rule and
triggers a full-suite run despite being neither new nor untested. The result is
SAFE but WRONG in its reasoning, and it fires on ordinary edits to model files,
which undermines the value of change-based selection precisely where it should
be cheapest. Worse, the fallback message will tell the user the file is new when
it is not.

NOTE THE ASYMMETRY: total_branches is derived from coverage's per-file analysis,
so a branchless file contributes nothing to the denominator either. Nothing is
miscounted -- the file is simply invisible.

OPTIONS.
1. Record a separate per-test file set alongside branches_covered, populated
   from the arc table's file_id for every executed arc regardless of whether it
   is a branch. Cheap: the ingest already streams every arc row, and the profile
   grows by roughly one path per test-file pair.
2. Distinguish 'file has no branches' from 'file not in the map' so so-jr5 can
   answer for branchless files without the full-suite fallback.

Option 1 also removes so-jr5's dependence on branch data for its file mapping,
which is a better fit for a feature whose granularity is deliberately
file-level.

WHERE: smoke_optimiser/profiler/coverage_db.py::read_coverage_db (the per-arc
loop already has file_id in hand); smoke_optimiser/profiler/models.py for the
profile format.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that imports and calls into a branchless module can be found
by asking the map which tests touched that module's file.
close_reason: Added per-test files_covered and top-level measured_files to the profile

title: Coverage recorded during fixture setup aborts the entire profiling run
description:
REGRESSION introduced by so-mr0. A single test whose fixture executes measured source and then errors kills the whole profiling run.

REPRODUCED 2026-09-06 on a 2-test throwaway project:

  @pytest.fixture
  def broken():
      classify(-1)                 # exercises measured source during setup
      raise RuntimeError('boom')

  def test_setup_error(broken): ...

  $ smoke-optimiser --src app
  1 passed, 1 error in 0.02s
  ❌ Error: 1 coverage context matches no test that pytest collected in this run:
    test_edge.py::test_setup_error

WHY. coverage records a context per test PHASE, so the fixture's coverage lands
under 'test_edge.py::test_setup_error|setup'. But PYTEST_HOOK_CODE in
runner.py only records a report when report.when == 'call':

    if report.when == 'call':
        item.config._smoke_outcomes[item.nodeid] = {...}

A test that errors during setup never reaches its call phase, so it is absent
from test_durations. coverage_db._verify_contexts then finds a context matching
no collected test and raises, by design -- that fail-loudly check is correct and
should stay. The bug is that the test IS real and WAS collected; the hook simply
did not record it.

TWO THINGS ARE WRONG.
1. One errored fixture takes down a whole profiling run of any size.
2. The error message misdiagnoses it, telling the user the coverage database is
   stale and to 'remove it and profile again', which will fail identically.

NOT A PROBLEM: skipped tests, and setup errors in fixtures that touch no
measured source, both produce no context row at all (verified), so they do not
trigger this.

LIKELY FIX. Record setup/teardown phase reports in the hook so such tests appear
with passed=False. Failing tests are already hard-excluded by the optimiser
(PRD 5.5), so an errored test would be excluded by the existing path rather than
being a fatal ingest error. Needs a decision on duration (setup time only? zero?)
and on whether a teardown failure after a passing call should flip passed.

WHERE: smoke_optimiser/profiler/runner.py PYTEST_HOOK_CODE; the check is
smoke_optimiser/profiler/coverage_db.py::_verify_contexts.

ACCEPTANCE: a suite containing a fixture that errors after touching measured
source profiles successfully, and tests/test_e2e.py covers it -- the current e2e
project has only cleanly-passing tests and would not catch this.
close_reason: Fixed by recording failed setup/teardown-phase reports in the pytest hook, so setup-erroring tests get an outcome entry instead of leaving an orphaned coverage context. Added regression coverage in tests/test_e2e.py.

title: Select tests from the map: turn a git diff and a profile into a test set
description:
smoke-optimiser's existing smoke mode selects a STATIC subset -- highest coverage
per second, the same tests whatever you changed. That is a coverage bet: it cannot
promise the coverage it skips, so it cannot gate a commit.

This is the second, honest selection mode. Given the files changed in the working
tree, run every test the profile says could be affected, and run the full suite
wherever the map cannot answer. The promise is categorical and literally statable,
which is the whole point: every test that has ever executed a line you touched,
plus every test that transitively imports a file you touched.

WHY IT IS POSSIBLE. The profiling data already IS a test-impact map.
ProfilingOutcome.files_covered gives file -> tests directly, and ImportGraph.edges
gives the dependency relation that answers for a file which only ever runs at
import time -- a constants module, a Pydantic model, a package re-export -- which
coverage records under no test context at all.

MEASURED on enphase_curtailer: 2600 tests, 190 files in the map, MEDIAN 37 TESTS
PER FILE. Touch one source file and you run ~37 of 2600. The full suite is 55s
warm on a 10-core Mac and 7m32s on GitHub CI's 4 cores.

GRANULARITY: FILE-LEVEL. Deliberately not line-level. Line numbers shift the moment
you insert a line above, so a line-level map silently mismatches after almost any
edit. File-level is immune to line shifts, reformatting and refactors within a
file. so-aif is the deferred line-level follow-up.

THE MAP MUST NEVER GUESS. Every input is either answered from recorded fact or
declared unanswerable, and unanswerable means the full suite with a stated reason.
There is no best-effort middle: the moment it selects a subset it cannot justify it
is test-fast again and cannot gate a commit.

SELF-HEALING. A full-suite fallback runs under profiling instrumentation and
rewrites the profile, so the run that pays for the fallback is also the run that
repairs the map. Instrumentation costs +11% (measured on enphase: 61s -> 68s), and
it means staleness costs one full run rather than accumulating until someone
remembers to regenerate by hand. Nothing regenerates in the background, and no
regeneration the developer did not ask for ever blocks a commit.

DOES NOT COVER, and must not pretend to: npm/vitest suites, tsc typechecks, codegen
drift checks, Rust. In casey_ai the heavy precommit item is a Docker integration
suite; only the Python half is in scope here.

This issue is the shared spec. Its children carry the work.
design:
THE INPUT is the union of staged, unstaged and untracked changes, because pytest
reads the worktree rather than the index: selecting on the index alone would test
something other than what is about to run. Renames are detected (-M) and resolved
to the OLD path, the only path the profile knows. A deleted file is looked up in
the map exactly like any other change -- the tests that executed it are the ones
most likely to break -- so nothing may gate on whether a path still exists on disk.

PATHS ARE REPO-RELATIVE throughout, from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, so the
profile and git agree by construction rather than by coincidence of the directory
smoke-optimiser was invoked from.

SELECTION for a changed file is the union of:
  - tests whose files_covered contains it (it executed under that test), and
  - tests whose module transitively imports it, via the inverted ImportGraph.

UNANSWERABLE -- run the full suite, and say which input caused it:
  - a changed path with no entry in the map (new code, which is exactly when tests
    matter most);
  - a changed path that is not Python at all (YAML, templates, assets, lockfiles,
    workflows). The map is a Python-execution map, so absence carries no
    information about a data file: it means "we never looked", not "nothing reads
    this". so-n6b.4 makes these answerable for real;
  - a changed file listed in ImportGraph.unattributed_modules, which means the
    graph is blind to who depends on it;
  - a profile whose map has never seen a file that exists now (see EXPIRY);
  - an import graph carrying failures we could not localise (see TRUST).

A CHANGED conftest.py selects every test at or below its directory, mirroring
pytest's own scoping rule, so a root conftest.py selects the whole suite and a
leaf one does not. A changed test file selects the tests in that file; a test file
that other tests import from is covered by the import graph like any other module.

EXPIRY is divergence, not age. A profile is expired once a file exists that its map
has never seen, because from that moment the map can answer confidently and wrongly:
the tests added since capture are absent from every answer it gives. Divergence is
a cliff rather than a slope, and the self-healing fallback is what makes the cliff
affordable -- hitting it costs one instrumented full run, not a full run on every
commit until someone regenerates by hand.

TRUST. The import tracer swallows and counts edge-resolution failures, because
raising inside __import__ would kill the suite being profiled. Every such failure
is our defect, not the project's -- it is our name arithmetic failing on legal
Python -- so the user must not be made to pay a full suite for it. The failure loses
the IMPORTED name while the IMPORTER is still in hand, so the doubt localises to
the importer: selection always additionally runs every test whose closure reaches a
module with a failed edge. Failures where even the importer could not be recovered
are counted separately and do force the full suite, since there is nothing to
localise them to.

OUTPUT is its own file with its own schema and its own pytest flag. The categorical
promise has no time cap, no coverage target and no efficiency ranking, so it shares
nothing with SmokeSuiteFile but the list of node ids.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED, and rejected -- do not re-propose without new evidence:

  - Staged-only input (--cached). Rejected: pytest runs against the worktree, so an
    unstaged edit changes what the selected tests execute.
  - Treating a rename's new path as unknown, or forgoing -M so it appears as an
    add plus a delete. Both make every pure move cost a full suite.
  - A user-configurable ignore list for non-Python paths, so a README edit does not
    cost a full run. Rejected: "this path is irrelevant" is a claim that should be
    MEASURED, not asserted -- an asserted list is silent under-selection the moment
    it is wrong. so-n6b.3 measures it instead.
  - Wall-clock expiry with a configured threshold. Rejected: it is a heuristic that
    reads a day of heavy refactoring as fresh and an untouched fortnight as stale,
    while divergence measures the thing that actually breaks the map.
  - Refusing any profile with non-zero resolution_errors. Rejected: it punishes the
    user durably for our bug, since the failures are deterministic and persist
    until we fix the tracer.
  - Trusting a degraded graph with only a warning. Rejected: that is the silent
    under-selection this whole line of work exists to prevent.
  - Printing node ids for the caller to pass to pytest, with no file. Rejected: it
    puts a full suite's worth of argv on the command line at 2600 tests, and the
    fallback must run through our entry point for the self-healing rewrite to
    happen at all.
  - Regenerating the profile in a detached background process. Rejected: a full
    suite firing at an unpredictable moment is worse than the instrumented
    fallback, which pays the cost exactly when the developer was already paying it.
acceptance_criteria: Changing a source file runs exactly the tests that executed it plus the tests whose modules transitively import it, and no others. Changing a file absent from the map, a non-Python file, an unattributed module, or a file in a repository whose map has never seen some existing file, runs the full suite and names the input that caused it. Changing tests/sub/conftest.py runs every test under tests/sub/ and nothing outside it. A deleted file still selects the tests that executed it. A full-suite fallback rewrites the profile, so an immediately repeated run selects a subset instead of falling back again.
notes:
WHAT THE PROFILE PROVIDES, and what each part is for:

  - ProfilingOutcome.files_covered: every measured file a test executed, branchless
    files included, so a straight-line constants module is visible where
    branches_covered cannot see it.
  - ProfilingData.measured_files: everything coverage measured, executed or not, so
    "coverage never saw this file" is distinguishable from "no test ran it".
  - ImportGraph.edges: (importer, imported) as project-relative paths. Invert and
    take the transitive closure for every test module depending on a changed file.
  - ImportGraph.unattributed_modules: project files loaded that nothing was seen to
    import -- test modules, conftest.py, and any pytest11 plugin belonging to the
    project, since pytest loads entry-point plugins before any hook can watch. A
    change to one means the graph CANNOT ANSWER.
  - ImportGraph.resolution_errors / error_samples / failed_importers: edge recording
    that failed and was swallowed, because raising inside __import__ would kill the
    run being profiled.

Measured on smoke-optimiser itself: 91 edges, 17 unattributed of ~35 project files.

WHAT AN IMPORT CLOSURE SELECTS, as a percentage of the suite, per source file, from
a --collect-only prototype (2026-09-06):

  repo                tests  files   p25    median   p75    max     mean
  smoke-optimiser        81     19  18.5%   27.2%   48.1%  87.7%   33.3%
  casey_ai/api         1389    143  20.5%   47.7%   52.1%  96.5%   39.4%
  enphase_curtailer    2600    271   7.3%   12.8%   21.9%  93.2%   17.5%

The decisive case is casey_ai: db/models/common.py reaches 96.5% of the suite
(genuinely global -- running everything IS right), while db/models/interval.py and
db/models/task.py reach 3 tests each. Same directory, same kind of declaration file.
The graph tells them apart; a file-glob heuristic cannot.

CAVEAT: measured with --collect-only, so it misses imports made lazily inside test
bodies. Real closures may be marginally wider.
MVP, labelled touched-files-mvp: so-jr5.1, so-jr5.2, so-7hr, so-uom, so-jr5.4,
so-n6b.1, plus so-2os and so-qex. That is the whole path from a git diff to a pytest
run, with expiry included so the answer is trustworthy rather than merely fast.

It ships with three conservative stand-ins, each of which over-selects or errors
rather than under-selecting, and each of which is replaced by a named issue:

  - any changed conftest.py is unanswerable      -> so-017
  - any non-zero resolution_errors distrusts the graph -> so-n6b.2
  - the fallback runs plain pytest, regenerate by hand -> so-jr5.3
  - the command refuses to run outside the repository root -> so-746

Sequenced this way so the feature exists end to end early and gets exercised against
real edits, rather than being assembled correct-on-paper and met all at once.
close_reason: Superseded by so-n6b, which now carries this spec verbatim as its description, design and notes. Its children moved up to so-n6b: grouping by hierarchy was not carrying information, and the axis that matters is the touched-files-mvp label.

title: Replace the 1.2 GB JSON coverage ingest with a direct read of coverage.py's SQLite database
description:
smoke-optimiser cannot profile a medium suite today. Measured against
enphase_curtailer (2600 tests, 230 files) on 2026-09-06:

  coverage json --show-contexts    1.2 GB
  the same data as .coverage       29 MB      (40x smaller)
  the same report WITHOUT contexts 1.9 MB in 1.3s

parser.py:193 does a single json.load() of that 1.2 GB file, which needs many
GB of resident Python objects. The contexts are 99.8% of the file.

WHAT TO BUILD. Read coverage.py's SQLite database directly instead. One query
joining arc -> context -> file extracted the full test->arc map in 0.43s and
yielded exactly 2600 tests, matching the collected count:

  select context.context, file.path, arc.fromno, arc.tono
    from arc join context on arc.context_id = context.id
             join file    on arc.file_id    = file.id
   where context.context != ''

The public CoverageData API is NOT viable: set_query_contexts()/arcs() over 40
contexts took 6.51s, extrapolating to 13.4 minutes for this suite. Raw SQL is
~1900x faster. That is why this reads an internal schema.

TWO CORRECTNESS BUGS THIS FIXES.

1. parser.py:139 infers branch coverage: a test covers u->v if it executed line
   u and line v. That over-attributes -- both endpoints can execute without that
   arc ever being taken. The arc table holds real arcs, so the inference and its
   docstring caveat both go away.
2. TestResolver (parser.py:37-77) matches coverage contexts to node ids by
   endswith/startswith and by bare function name. Contexts are already exact node
   ids with a phase suffix ('tests/test_x.py::test_y|run'), so rsplit('|', 1)[0]
   is exact. The fuzzy matcher can mis-attribute coverage between same-named
   tests in different files; delete it.

SCHEMA COUPLING. The DB format is not a public API. Read the coverage_schema
table (version 7 as of coverage 7.13) and compare against a verified set. On a
mismatch, FAIL LOUDLY -- silently mis-reading would silently under-select tests,
which is the worst failure this tool can have. The error must name the schema
version found, the versions supported, the installed coverage.py version, and
say plainly that smoke-optimiser itself needs updating to support the new schema,
with the file to edit. Do not degrade quietly.

THE DENOMINATOR. The arc table records only arcs that were EXECUTED, so a
never-taken branch has no row. enphase has 3198 branches, 406 uncovered; counting
from SQLite alone reports 100% instead of 88%. --target-cov needs the true total,
so keep a SECOND context-free `coverage json` purely for totals -- 1.9 MB and 1.3s,
because the blow-up was entirely contexts. total_branches keeps its current
meaning (executed + missing).

Everything moves to the SQLite ingest, not just the new selection feature, so the
tool has one ingest path rather than two. Retire parse_coverage_json, TestResolver,
the CoverageReport/CoverageFile models, the [json] show_contexts rcfile setting,
and the contexts export step in runner.py:159-176.

Also handle a suite profiled WITHOUT branch mode: that data lands in line_bits
(a bitmap blob), not arc. Either support it or refuse with a clear message.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED with two departures from the original description, both agreed with the user.

1. NO SECOND coverage json. The description called for a context-free 'coverage json'
purely for the denominator. Not needed: the denominator is computed in-process from
coverage's own per-file analysis (FileReporter.arcs() filtered to branch lines), in the
same pass that builds the arc translation map. Measured 0.03s on this repo. Verified
byte-identical to 'coverage json' on both sets (denominator 234/234, executed 153/153),
and the 222-branch total matches pytest-cov's own report exactly. One ingest, no
subprocess, no JSON, no absolute-vs-relative path reconciliation between two sources.

2. RAW ARCS NEED TRANSLATING -- not mentioned in the original description, and the
landmine in it. The arc table records the interpreter's actual jump targets; coverage
reports branches in an AST-derived vocabulary. A jump into the middle of a multi-line
statement is reported against the statement's first line, so raw 3->6 is reported as
3->5. Intersecting raw arcs against reported branches without translation silently
dropped ~4% of this repo's executed branches -- exactly the silent under-selection the
issue exists to prevent. Fixed by running each file's distinct raw arcs through
FileReporter.translate_arcs ONCE, building a raw->branch lookup, then a dict hit per
arc. This is what sidesteps the 13.4-minute per-context path.

3. UNATTRIBUTABLE BRANCHES. Module-level code runs at import under the empty context,
so no test can ever claim it (4 branches on this repo). The old inference-based parser
falsely attributed these to whichever test touched the lines. They are now kept in
total_branches (so it keeps agreeing with 'coverage report') and surfaced as a new
ProfilingData.unattributable_branches field, with the summary reporting the attainable
ceiling: 'Ceiling: 98.2% max attainable'.

FAIL-LOUDLY paths, all tested: unsupported coverage_schema version (names version found,
supported set, installed coverage.py, and the file to edit), line-only data (has_arcs=0),
a context matching no collected test, a source file no longer readable, a corrupt or
non-coverage database, an empty coverage_schema table.

FOR so-jr5: branch ids are relative to project_root (POSIX), so they match git diff paths
directly. Note the file->test map only covers files that contain branches.
close_reason: Implemented: SQLite ingest with arc translation, in-process denominator, fail-loudly schema and context checks. Verified byte-identical to coverage json; 76 tests pass; ruff/ty clean.

title: Version the profile file, so an incompatible profile says so instead of failing as a validation error
description:
ProfilingDataFile (profiler/models.py) carries no schema version. .smoke_suite.json has had one since it was written -- version: int = 1 plus generator_version (reports/smoke_suite.py:53-55) -- but the profile the downwind maps are built from has none.

The gap is already visible in the code. cli.py:115-119 catches a ValidationError while loading .smoke_profiling_data.json and tells the user 'If this profile was recorded by an older version, re-run the profiling phase to regenerate it' -- a diagnosis the data cannot support. The loader has no way to distinguish an old profile from a corrupt one, so it guesses, and the user sees a Pydantic field trace rather than a statement about what is wrong and what to do.

This stops being cosmetic the moment so-n6b.1 lands. so-n6b.14 settled that the profile records the scope roots it was captured under, and that a profile with no recorded scope is a hard error rather than a silent full-suite run. Without a version, 'no recorded scope' is indistinguishable from 'malformed file', and the error cannot name the fix.
